ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2021, together with Companies Regulation 32A and Form CoR 42.1 (statutory beneficial-ownership filing); Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001, as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Prevention of Organised Crime Act 121 of 1998; Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorism and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004; and the South African Reserve Bank and National Treasury sanctions reporting framework.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (the CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register is electronically filed and accessible to the Financial Intelligence Centre, CIPC, SARS, and law-enforcement authorities through defined statutory gateways; no unrestricted public search exists)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and/or certified copy of passport of every beneficial owner and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin or South African notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for HCCH contracting states); otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address of each beneficial owner (utility bill or bank statement dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing utility provider or bank, witnessed by a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for foreign-issued documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and good-standing certificate of any corporate shareholder
Signed consent to act as director (Form CoR 36.1) and executed memorandum of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required; executed locally and lodged with CIPC

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, directors, and senior officers against the South African FIC politically exposed persons (PEP) dataset (PEPs, their spouses, partners, and immediate family per FIC s. 21F), the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, UK OFSI, and EU restrictive measures; enhanced due diligence applies to high-risk jurisdictions per FATF standards and FIC guidance; ongoing transaction monitoring is required across the Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, and Stripe payment rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services Online Registry — Corporate Name Reservation Module (eservices.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be expressed in the Roman alphabet; the name may be in any of the 11 official languages of South Africa, but non-Latin-script names must be transliterated into the Roman alphabet; diacritical marks are permitted; a name must not be identical, confusingly similar, offensive, or likely to mislead the public.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: CIPC name reservations are valid for 365 days and are non-extendable; a lapsed reservation may be replaced by a fresh reservation application. Upon rejection, the applicant must (i) request written reasons via CIPC e-Services within 10 business days of the rejection notice; (ii) file a formal written objection and reconsideration request through the CIPC name-objection workflow within 20 business days of receipt of the reasons; and (iii) if unsuccessful, appeal to the Companies Tribunal under section 12(2) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, and thereafter apply for judicial review in the High Court under section 11(4) within the statutory prescription period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only where the virtual-office provider maintains an actual South African physical street address capable of receiving service of legal process and mail on behalf of the company; P.O. Box-only addresses and telephonic-only arrangements are impermissible under section 23(2) of the Companies Act. For the ISIC 5911 vertical micro-drama streaming industry, serviced-office and virtual registered-office arrangements are acceptable market practice.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — quantified at below 5% annual probability for a non-regulated, non-licensed low-risk private company. CIPC does not conduct routine unannounced physical site inspections for standard Pty Ltd incorporations; however, unannounced on-site verification may arise upon a SARS audit, B-BBEE verification, trade-mark or consumer complaint, or law-enforcement inquiry.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended, sections 13 (Incorporation of company), 14 (Memorandum of Incorporation), 23 (name), 28 (registered office), 66 (board of directors), and 69 (director appointments)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) together with Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital required; shareholder subscription as set out in the MOI. No escrow account or capital deposit required for incorporation under South African law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [•] PROPRIETARY LIMITED. The directors hereby: (i) accept the subscription of 100 ordinary shares in the company's authorized capital by the founding shareholder and issue these shares as fully paid-up; (ii) adopt the rental agreement for the pre-approved registered office at [physical address, Johannesburg, South Africa]; (iii) appoint [Name] as Director, [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, and [Name] as Company Secretary, each holding office per the Memorandum of Incorporation; (iv) declare that the initial share capital is in order; and (v) authorize the filing of this resolution with the Company minutes. Unanimous consent recorded. Date. Chairperson signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the Proposed Company Name with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), Name Reservation Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name reservation application (Form CoR 9.4) electronically through the CIPC e-Services portal. Search for name availability. If the name is unobjectionable and not similar to existing names, the name is reserved for 60 days.
required_dossiers: Identity document or passport of each authorized representative
Proof of payment of name reservation fee (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is flagged for similar or prohibited name, submit a fresh reservation with an alternative name within 60 days or file an application to the CIPC Name Committee for a determination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal drafting preparers (accredited law firm) and CIPC e-Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the MOI in accordance with Schedule 2 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008. Complete Form CoR 15.1 (Notice of Incorporation), including the company's registered address, number of directors, and addresses of directors. Both the MOI and Notice must be signed by each subscriber. Arrange for notarization if directors are absent or using alternative signature processes.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director forms (CoR 1.1)
Proof of identification for each founder/director
Power of attorney if signed by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOI is incomplete, CIPC will issue a defect notice. Rectify all omissions and resubmit through the e-services portal within 20 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Application and Pay Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the CoR 15.1 and MOI electronically. Use the 'Register a Company' transaction. The system validates all requirements, generates a payment reference, and upon payment acceptance, issues an automated receipt. The official fee is approximately ZAR 475 (USD 25).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, CIPC provides written reasons. Correct deltas and file a new application, or lodge a notice of objection with the CIPC within 15 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Registration Certificate and Company Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The CIPC will issue a Certificate of Incorporation, assigning a unique company registration number. The certificate is digitally signed and available for download in PDF.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed, request an expedited issuance via the CIPC call centre or file a complaint on the CIPC case management system.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Revenue Taxes with the South African Revenue Service (SARS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the 'Relevant Material' via SARS eFiling. Register for Income Tax, Value-Added Tax (if taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1 million), Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE), Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF), and Skills Development Levy (SDL). Provide the company's registration number and bank details.
required_dossiers: Letter of authorization for tax practitioner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS rejects the application, agents can file a corrected registration on eFiling or visit the closest SARS branch with supporting documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a Local Corporate Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks (e.g., First National Bank, Standard Bank, or ABSA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the corporate bank account opening form together with a certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation and MOI. Complete the beneficial ownership declaration per the Financial Intelligence Centre Act. The directors must appear in person for the identification and KYC verification.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional information, provide corrected resolutions or certified translations; file a formal objection to the bank's FIC review within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Maintain Statutory Records and Company Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Set up a Company Register with the following records: share register, register of directors, register of beneficial ownership, and minutes of board meetings. File the annual return (CoR 36.1) with CIPC each year by the anniversary of incorporation. Conduct an annual shareholders meeting as per the MOI.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return is overdue, lodge the outstanding return and file a compelling reason for late submission; CIPC may impose penalties. Reinstatement can be applied for if status is 'Denied Dissolvement'.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Municipal Operational and Physical Clearance (if operating physical premises)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Johannesburg Department of Development Planning and the District Fire Brigade
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal trading/occupational certificate by submitting a zoning certificate, built plan, and proof of right of occupancy. For premises that will house a production studio, schedule an electrical and building inspection. Obtain a Fire Safety certificate from the Fire Brigade and occupational inspection from the Department of Employment and Labour.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal application is refused, appeal to the Municipal Ombudsman, or correct identified structural deficiencies and resubmit the inspected reports.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Film and Publication Board (FPB) for content distribution; local municipality for physical premises only. No industrial manufacturing licensing board applies to OTT/VoD digital streaming platforms.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not mandatory for pure digital short drama distribution; voluntary FPB distributor classification registration. If operating a physical studio, a municipal Trade and Occupational Certificate is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) / Provincial Environmental Affairs
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no listing under NEMA EIA Regulations for pure content distribution; a Basic Assessment is only required if constructing a studio or modifying a heritage building.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to digital operations. If a physical studio is established, comply with National Water Act (GN 399) discharge standards and National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act (NEM:AQA) for VOC emissions below 100 kg/year threshold.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate per SANS 10400 and civil defense regulations; mechanical/electrical compliance to OHS Act Section 8 (DEE) and Certificate of Occupancy issued by the municipality.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); official portal: SARS eFiling (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A South African Proprietary Limited company is incorporated via the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) with a CIPC registration number. SARS automatically creates the income tax reference number (TRN) through verified CIPC data integration; if not generated, the company registers on SARS eFiling with the CIPC certificate, Memorandum of Incorporation and directors' identification. The company must register for VAT as a vendor under VAT Act No. 89 of 1991 via form VAT101 on eFiling once taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any rolling 12-month period, or voluntarily from ZAR 50,000. Foreign entities contracting with the SA company without a local branch appoint a registered SARS practitioner/representative and file the non-resident registration pack (certified founding documents, foreign tax residency certificate, board resolutions) to obtain a non-resident TRN and, if required, a VAT vendor number. Separate customs registration (importer/exporter code with SAD500/SASEC electronic access) is completed through the SARS Customs Modernisation system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not provide a check-the-box classification election; a resident (Pty) Ltd is automatically taxed at entity level at 27% corporate income tax under the Income Tax Act No. 58 of 1962. Available statutory elections include: VAT group registration under s.23K of the VAT Act; corporate restructuring rollover elections under ss.44-46 of the Income Tax Act; dividend tax exemption election under s.10(1)(k)(i); and the hybrid mismatch integrity rules in ss.23M-23T of the Income Tax Act, which restrict deduction-conferring classification elections in cross-border app-store and licensor structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) - Value-Added Tax Act No. 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 in taxable supplies in a rolling 12-month period (compulsory); voluntary registration from ZAR 50,000; foreign suppliers of electronic services use the same ZAR 1,000,000 compulsory threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or per-invoice pre-approval regime is currently in force in South Africa. SARS is phasing in PEPPOL-based electronic invoicing on a voluntary, pre-approved basis. VAT invoices must comply with s.20 of the VAT Act (full prescribed particulars, including the SARS 15-digit VAT registration number, supply date, consideration, VAT amount and zero-rated indication) and be issued within the statutory time frame. The entity must reconcile Apple IAP/Google Play/Stripe settlement reports to its VAT201 declarations; SARS may require submission of e-commerce transaction-level data via eFiling APIs during audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: a vendor may zero-rate exported goods under s.11(1)(d) of the VAT Act where the sale is to a recipient outside South Africa and the goods are physically removed from South Africa within the period and under the documentary conditions prescribed by s.11(3). Services: zero-rating under s.11(2)(l) of the VAT Act for services rendered in South Africa to a non-resident who is not in the Republic at the time of supply, and under s.11(2)(k) for services supplied to a non-resident for business purposes outside the Republic; exclusions apply where services relate to South African immovable or movable property. For vertical micro-drama streaming sold through Apple/Google app stores, zero-rating is supportable where the end-user supply chain is documented as non-resident, the app-store counterparty is the billing agent resident outside South Africa, and South African consumer demand is standard-rated at 15%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: SAD500 Customs Export Declaration / SASEC electronic export declaration (physical goods only)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical exportation (where applicable)
Commercial invoice and signed digital distribution agreement with the non-resident app-store operator (Apple/Google) or non-resident customer
App-store settlement report/sales statement showing platform fees, territorial sales, device residency and non-resident attribution
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or authorised dealer bank statement evidencing that foreign currency sales proceeds were repatriated to the South African bank account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS audits will review the s.11(3) evidence bundle and territorial app-store data; on failure, zero-rating is reversed and the supply attracts 15% VAT with statutory interest. Additional tax under s.60 of the VAT Act may be imposed up to 100% of the tax (up to 200% where non-disclosure/false declaration was made with intent to evade tax). Understatement penalties under s.223 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 may reach 150% of the shortfall, with monthly administrative non-compliance penalties in addition. Fraudulent export invoicing or forged IRC/customs documentation constitutes criminal tax evasion under s.234 TAA (fine and/or imprisonment up to 2 years per count), triggers retrospective refund clawback, and may be reported to the South African Reserve Bank for exchange-control violations (non-repatriation within 180 days).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) - Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act 9 of 1933), the Exchange Control Regulations, and delegated powers to Authorised Dealers (licensed commercial banks).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The ZAR operates under a managed-float regime. Current-account convertibility is unrestricted for service exports; digital-content and vertical micro-drama streaming receipts are freely convertible to ZAR through an Authorised Dealer without prior SARB consent. Capital-account inflows (non-resident equity subscription) require no SARB pre-approval for a non-affected (Pty) Ltd, but must be recorded via Form A at the receiving bank and will be subject to source-of-funds KYC under FICA. Dividend and profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted upon: (i) issuance of a SARS Tax Compliance Status (TCS) PIN; (ii) proof of the original inward capital in the bank's Foreign Liability/Form A records; and (iii) compliance with annual Exchange Control reporting. The main practical hurdle is not foreign-exchange restriction but the SARS TCS gate, which forces full corporate tax and VAT compliance before any distribution is effected offshore.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The statutory repatriation timeline for exported services is 180 days from the date of invoicing/rendering. The mandatory conversion ratio is 100% of the foreign-currency export proceeds contractually due; partial conversion or deferred conversion requires FinSurv/Authorised Dealer consent granted via an approved Foreign Currency Account (rare for services). Where Apple, Google, and Stripe net their fees before remittance, the export proceeds are the net credited amounts evidenced by platform settlement statements; the bank will expect that every net remittance is converted to ZAR through the Authorised Dealer and reconciled to the corresponding platform report. A 180-day breach is an Exchange Control contravention carrying administrative penalties and, in persistent cases, referral to the National Prosecuting Authority, plus quarantine of the foreign account by the Authorised Dealer.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Medium with binding legal constraints. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise Business, Airwallex, Payoneer, Currencycloud) may be used as short-cycle collection accounts for Apple/Google/Stripe settlements, but cannot replace an Authorised Dealer: they are not licensed by SARB/FinSurv to convert ZAR, issue Form A records, or evidence 180-day surrender compliance. A lawful structure is: (i) collect foreign-currency app-store settlements into the EMI; (ii) sweep accumulated balances via SWIFT MT103 to the SA Authorised Dealer when the balance exceeds a minimum FX threshold; (iii) present EMI/platform statements to the bank for export-proceeds reconciliation. Any direct ZAR conversion by an unlicensed EMI would breach Exchange Control Regulations and trigger FICA reporting obligations. Reliance on a sole EMI as primary bank account is therefore inadvisable and materially increases AML underwriting risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: South African FICA permits remote onboarding; physical presence is not a statutory requirement. Tier-1 banks, however, will require an interactive video interview with at least one director and notarised/apostilled certified copies of identity documents for any non-resident director. Where no director holds South African tax residence or a local phone/business address, the bank escalates onboarding to its Group Compliance Committee; the timeline extends to 4-8 weeks and may demand a correspondent-bank reference or an in-person branch visit. A faster path (1-3 weeks) is available where the company appoints a resident director, company secretary, or authorised FICA officer who can complete the branch interview and accept service. For the ISIC 5911 vertical-drama entity with a fully non-resident board, the recommendation is to place one executive director in Johannesburg/Cape Town or appoint a licensed corporate services provider to satisfy the interview and ongoing contact obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity on the non-resident equity injection (e.g., remittances from a third party or an intermediary corporate account rather than the UBO's personal banking account)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised share subscription agreement; certified board resolution; UBO source-of-wealth declaration; bank reference from the investor's home bank; full SWIFT MT103 remitter-beneficiary matching; a signed third-party payment waiver plus passport copy of the beneficial owner where a third party pays.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of ZAR 100 per month or part thereof; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers CIPC administrative strike-off/deregistration, suspension of corporate legal capacity, and cessation of trading rights.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Annual Confirmation (s26B and s33)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC (filed with or confirmed during the annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the CIPC annual return; changes in beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days of the company becoming aware
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC annual return will not be accepted without beneficial ownership confirmation; non-compliance is an offence under the Companies Act and may result in administrative penalties, refusal of annual return processing, and continued default may lead to deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 12 months after the end of each financial year, unless SARS prescribes a different annual filing due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly administrative non-compliance penalty under the Tax Administration Act; SARS may issue an estimated assessment, impose understatement penalties up to 100%-200% of the tax shortfall, suspend tax clearance, and commence civil collection proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory audit applies to public or state-owned companies and to any company with a Public Interest Score (PIS) of 350 or more. A company with PIS 100-349 requires an independent review if its annual financial statements are internally compiled. This private micro company is below the 100-point threshold and therefore is not subject to audit or independent review unless its Memorandum of Incorporation or shareholders require otherwise.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB; private companies may apply IFRS for SMEs. Legacy South African GAAP is not generally permitted for current annual reporting periods.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register and submit the annual beneficial ownership information with the CIPC annual return each year. Any shareholding transfer or other change in beneficial ownership must be recorded and reported to CIPC within 30 days of the company becoming aware of the change. The annual confirmation is mandatory even in a year with no shareholding movement.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Prescribed Officers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 90 - 250 per year for a standard registered office and corporate secretarial service in South Africa
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required for this micro private company unless PIS reaches 350 or a shareholder mandate arises; if mandated, a small-company statutory audit typically costs USD 2,000 - 6,000 per year

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying Small Business Corporations (SBC) pay a graduated rate: 0% on the first ±ZAR 95,750 of taxable income, then 7% and 21% bands, with the 27% headline rate applying above ±ZAR 550,000. Section 11D research-and-development deductions and Section 12O film-investment deductions are available for qualifying expenditure; South Africa grants no general tax holidays.
